issue.title: Credit bead reopens to the acting reopener instead of the creator
issue.description:
PROPOSED BY phase sase-19p.1 note #1 while implementing agent-close attribution. This is an independent, out-of-scope attribution defect; epic sase-19p fixes close events only.

In sase-core `crates/sase_core/src/bead/mutation/close_remove.rs`, `open_issue` appends `IssueOpened` with `&issue.created_by` and `reopen_closed_ancestors` appends each ancestor's `IssueOpened` with `&ancestor.created_by`. The API has no acting-reopener parameter. The touch index maps `IssueOpened` to `reopened` by the envelope actor, so the bead creator gets credit for a different agent's reopen. Ancestor creators are likewise credited when reopening cascades.

Reproduce in a temporary bead store: create a bead as agent A, close it, reopen it as agent B, refresh the touch index, then compare `sase bead history` and `sase bead touched --json` for both agents. The opened event and `reopened` touch name A. Include a closed parent and child to cover automatic ancestor reopening. Pass the acting reopener through the Rust mutation and binding, Python CLI, and any other agent-facing call path; human actions should fall back to the store owner. Add regression tests for direct and ancestor reopens. This source was rechecked on sase-core HEAD 9d049aa during sase-19p landing.

task_type_fields.impact: Agent history and Context Beads rows falsely credit creators with reopens performed by another agent.
task_type_fields.repro: Agent B reopens a bead created by A; IssueOpened actor and the touch-index reopened verb are attributed to A. Closed ancestor reopens similarly credit the ancestor creator.
